title: Review of c52's digestion ecology on fresh seed 5: S, X and the predators' E replicate and predators persist and divide (87 persistent tracks, 40 persistent splits, generation 3), but 89% of predator bodies touch a prey body, so the predator-prey pair may be the individual
summary: Seed 5, 256^2, t=12000, defaults, K=20 frames: predators 147 bodies on average (187 at the end), 87 persistent tracks, 69 splits, 40 persistent (generation 3), merge/split 0.20, 309 moving tracks; prey 177 on average, 104 persistent tracks, 67 persistent splits (generation 4), merge/split 0.40. Predator-free twin (same seed and grid): 158 prey, 157 persistent tracks, 0 splits, 0 moving tracks. attach.py: of 17966 predator components (>= 4 px, frames 20-119), 16040 (89%) touch a prey body within 2 px; about 19 of ~180 per frame are free. Prey removal at t=6000 (128^2, labkit, dfork_t 6000): predators 46/45/31/4/0 at t=6000/6200/6400/6600/6800, max c_b 1.57 -> 0.50 by t=6800, mean c_b 0.111 -> 0.100; fed run (same seed) keeps 46-54 predators.

observations.S: pack256_s5/sheet.png t=0: smoothed noise in prey material over the whole box; predator material added as noise over the whole box at t=2000
observations.X: twin256_s5 (pred_on 0): 158 frozen prey, 0 splits, 0 moving tracks; with predators 67 persistent prey splits and 320 moving prey tracks (pack256_s5/FACTS.md)
observations.E: dfork128_s5: predators 46 -> 0 within 800 t of prey removal, predator material not removed by the code (mean c_b 0.111 -> 0.100); fed128_s5 keeps 46-54
observations.I: pack256_s5/FACTS.md: 87 persistent predator tracks; comet-shaped predator bodies on prey (sheet t>=2600)
observations.D: pack256_s5/lineage.png: 40 persistent predator splits, generation 3; prey 67, generation 4

seeds_run.result: pass for the counts, the twin contrast and the prey-removal fork

verdicts.limitation: I mark the verdict Weak for the same reason as my review of c43's CIPS consumer, though the case is stronger here: 89% of predator bodies touch a prey body at every frame and, by the author's own strict test, predator divisions happen with prey within 6 px, so I, D and E may belong to a prey-predator pair rather than to the predator alone; unlike the CIPS consumer, labkit does track the predators as persistent bodies (87). Prey merge/split is 0.40 on this seed (reticulate prey genealogy, near the rubric's 50% line). The prey-removal fork is at 128^2 and I did not run the fuel fork for the prey's E. The taxis is a written nonreciprocal drift, as the author states. My sheet is too coarse to show individual joint fissions; I rely on the author's strips for their shape.
